This Quick 4-Ingredient Pasta Is the Weeknight Dinner I Keep Coming Back To
5.0
(3)
2 Reviews

It’s packed with veggies, but you barely need to chop a thing.
By Alexandra Shytsman
Published on May 19, 2026

Pasta with tomatoes and spinach in a skillet
Credit:

Simply Recipes / Alexandra Shytsman

    This easy pasta gets dinner on the table in 25 minutes with barely any prep work.
    Burst cherry tomatoes and sliced garlic build a glossy sauce while the pasta cooks.
    Short pasta shapes hold onto the chunky tomato spinach sauce instead of it getting lost.
    You can use parmesan cheese or nutritional yeast to finish the dish for a flexible dairy-free option.

In the realm of quick-cooking vegetables, baby spinach and cherry tomatoes reign supreme—hence why they are permanent fixtures of my grocery list and subsequently, my weeknight dinners.

Baby spinach literally requires zero prep work (not even washing!) and wilts in record time, making it practically foolish not to add greens to your soups, noodles, beans, etc. Same goes for mini tomatoes. In many cases, you can skip chopping them, too.

Which brings me to this ultra easy veggie dinner. This tomato spinach pasta comes together in the time it takes to boil a box of pasta, and it’s likely you already have everything you need to make it right in your kitchen.
Bowl of pasta with spinach tomato and grated cheese

Simply Recipes / Alexandra Shytsman
What’s in This Easy Pasta

While the pasta water comes to a boil and the pasta cooks, you blister two containers of cherry tomatoes in a skillet and let the tomatoes collapse and release their juices, thus creating a sauce. Lots of sliced garlic goes in next, followed by baby spinach, the cooked pasta, and some pasta water.

The result: a garlicky veggie pasta full of sweet-savory tomato flavor and silky greens. The dish can be served as is, or finished with either a sprinkling of parmesan or nutritional yeast.
Ingredient Notes

    Although in many contexts cherry and grape tomatoes can be used interchangeably, in this case, I really recommend cherry tomatoes. They are typically juicier and create a saucier pasta.
    This chunky pasta is much better suited to short pasta shapes. Go for fusilli corti bucati like I do, or another non-tubular option, like orecchiette, cavatelli, or small shells.
    Not sure what to do with leftover dry pasta? Save it for soup!
    If you don’t enjoy heat, skip the red pepper flakes.

Pasta dish with tomato sauce spinach and grated cheese served in a white bowl with a fork

Simply Recipes / Alexandra Shytsman
More 20-Minute Pastas to the Rescue

    Quick Tuna Pasta
    Broccoli Pesto Pasta
    5-Ingredient Barbecue Chicken Pasta
    Spring Carbonara

Prep Time:
5 mins
Cook Time:
20 mins
Total Time:
25 mins
Servings:
4 servings
Keep Screen Awake
Ingredients

    Salt and freshly ground black pepper

    12 ounces (3/4 of a standard package) short pasta, such as fusilli corti bucati, orecchiette, cavatelli, or small shells)

    3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

    2 pints cherry tomatoes (about 4 cups)

    6 medium cloves garlic, thinly sliced

    1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes, optional

    1 (5-ounce) container baby spinach

    Grated parmesan cheese or nutritional yeast, for serving, optional

Directions

    Cook the pasta:

    Bring a medium pot of water to a boil over high heat. Salt the boiling water generously and cook the pasta until it is just short of al dente according to the package directions (it will finish cooking in the sauce). Scoop out 1/2 cup of the pasta cooking water right before draining the pasta.
    Meanwhile, cook the tomatoes:

    While the water is coming up to a boil, in a large high-sided skillet, combine the oil, tomatoes, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cover tightly with a lid and place over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have burst and released their juices, about 10 minutes.
    Finish the sauce:

    Using the back of a wooden spoon, lightly smash the tomatoes to help them collapse. Then, add the garlic, red pepper flakes (if using), and lots of freshly ground black pepper. Cook, uncovered and stirring often, until the sauce thickens slightly, about 2 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until most of it is wilted, about 1 minute.
    Finish and serve:

    Add the hot drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce, along with the reserved pasta cooking water. Stir to combine and cook just until the pasta is al dente and lightly coated in sauce, about 2 more minutes.

    Serve the pasta immediately, sprinkled with parmesan or nutritional yeast, if desired.

    Love the recipe? Leave us stars and a comment below!
    Plate of pasta with spinach tomatoes and grated cheese fork placed on the side pan partially visible on the left

    Simply Recipes / Alexandra Shytsman
